A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same rotation-symmetry method for transformer fusion. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, proofs and appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original NLP and image-classification fusion results, parameter-distance measurements, runtime measurements and layer-subset experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds ViT comparator results, component ablations and loss-landscape measurements.

M1.justification: FFN permutation matching, attention rotation matching and subsequent rescaling remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text. The correction to Equation 11 agrees with v1's existing Equation 12 and parameter updates, supporting a mathematical correction rather than a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same emotion-classification, NER, CoNLL transfer, CIFAR-10 and GLUE coverage. The added analyses reuse the existing pretrained ViT pair and image-classification setting; they introduce no new dataset, domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds OT-ACTS and OT-WTS to the ViT fusion comparisons. The earlier OT comparator is the retained OT-ACTS-EMD, not another addition. The NLP comparator set and the Git Re-Basin/OT-Fusion distance comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds component-removal accuracy controls and cross-entropy measurements along linear parameter interpolation in Section 5.4. Existing training and benchmark protocols remain unchanged. The distance plot relabels the unchanged 640.01/639.96 values from attention-only to 'w/o ATTN' settings without explanation, leaving those configurations unclear.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds downstream-accuracy ablations excluding attention or FFN matching across six ViT fusion methods. Section 5.4 and Figure 5 add a four-condition loss-landscape and barrier study. These substantially extend the component and connectivity evidence beyond v1's retained distance, rescaling and layer-subset analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting; the loss-barrier arrows do not represent statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: New results substantially extend the empirical findings: OT-ACTS reports 61.15 accuracy without matching versus 61.25 with full matching, and Figure 5 reports corresponding loss barriers of 2.295 versus 2.208. New ablations show that Fisher attention-only matching scores 20.21, exceeding full matching's 18.58. Tables 1 and 3 and the retained Table 2 results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 11 replaces incorrectly repeated query terms in the reciprocal-scaling penalties with key terms, repairing its inconsistency with Equation 12. Theorem 4.1, its Appendix A proof and the complexity analysis remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: continuous rotation symmetry, theoretically optimal parameter matching, and efficient improvement of transformer fusion across NLP and vision. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the brief limitations paragraph with substantial qualifications concerning pairwise versus multi-model optimality, incomplete symmetry coverage, general invertible transformations and the lack of joint rotation/rescaling optimality. Sections 5.3–5.4 also add component-specific and loss-landscape interpretations. The same-architecture assumption remains in Section 4.1.

D1.justification: Appendix C identifies separate NLP and vision implementation sources and supplies repository links for both; v1's baseline implementation statement only referenced Jin et al. The paper's own code link, software versions, hardware and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on parameter symmetry, recent model merging and metanetworks, including a short discussion connecting the work to permutation-equivariant neural functionals. Baseline descriptions are expanded, while the substantive positioning against Git Re-Basin, OT-ACTS and Tran et al. remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained. Local revisions standardize terminology, add a research question and loss-landscape subsection, move Algorithm 1 into the main text, reorganize the appendices and expand baseline and limitations explanations. Publication and acknowledgment text is also added.

P2.justification: v2 adds a six-panel ablation figure and a loss-landscape plot with a barrier table, redraws Figure 2, and transposes and expands Table 2. Algorithm 1 is relocated and reformatted. The existing distance plot is relabeled as Figure 4, while the layer-subset plot is retained as Figure 6.

improvement.justification: The added component and loss-landscape evidence, corrected Equation 11, explicit optimality limitations and implementation links make v2 more informative and transparent. The gains are bounded: the method and original main results remain unchanged, uncertainty reporting is still absent, and the unexplained reversal of attention-only labels in the reused distance plot introduces ambiguity. Overall, the additional evidence and clearer qualifications support a limited net improvement.
